title: Sessioned progressive tool invocation patterns with TS/Python/Go examples
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Deliver a set of SDK patterns and concrete examples for session-scoped progressive outputs + tool/function invocation across TypeScript, Python, and Go. Goal: make it ergonomically easy to (1) consume partially-emitted structured outputs (incremental JSON fragments / events), (2) attach tool calls to a single session context (session id, resume/rewind semantics), and (3) provide backward-compatible shims that map existing callback/legacy APIs to the new progressive/sessioned surfaces.
design_decisions: Use a lightweight session token per invocation (session_id) that is returned by the server and used for resumable streaming or tool correlation.

Model progressive structured output as a stream of typed events rather than raw text deltas (EventKind: partial_json, tool_call, final_json, metadata). This keeps parsing robust with incremental parsing strategies.
Expose both pull-based (async iterator) and push-based (event handler) ergonomics in each SDK to fit host-language idioms.
Provide a compatibility adapter layer that converts legacy text-stream callbacks into the new event envelope so existing clients can upgrade incrementally.
Keep binary-safe framing minimal: newline-delimited JSON envelopes with an initial handshake event including session metadata.
Limit server-side session lifetime by default (60s) with explicit resume tokens for longer-running orchestrations; clients may request longer TTL in enterprise deployments.
Security: session tokens are short-lived, bound to the original API key, and audited — security review required before GA.
api_examples:
Python example - async generator + resume token:

from redwood import RedwoodClient, EventKind
import os
import json

client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['RW_KEY'])

async def orchestrate():
    resp = await client.invoke(model='gpt-x', inputs='Generate plan and call tools', session={'ttl_seconds': 90})
    session_id = resp['session_id']
    async for ev in resp['stream']:
        kind = ev['kind']
        if kind == EventKind.PARTIAL_JSON:
            # incremental parser can append string fragments safely
            partial_handler(ev['payload'])
        elif kind == EventKind.TOOL_CALL:
            # synchronous tool execution in Python example
            result = run_tool_sync(ev['tool_name'], ev['args'])
            await client.tool_response(session_id=session_id, call_id=ev['call_id'], result=result)
        elif kind == EventKind.FINAL_JSON:
            return json.loads(ev['payload'])

# Resume example (useful if the connection dropped)
# The server returns resume_token at start; pass resume_token to resume_stream() which replays missed events
acceptance_criteria: SDKs (TS/Python/Go) publish a stable sessioned streaming API with both iterator and event-handler consumption modes.
Tool invocation from streamed events is supported: server emits ToolCall events and SDK exposes toolResponse(session_id, call_id, result).
Compatibility adapter provided for legacy text-streaming callbacks with documented caveats (lossy flattening of structured partials).
End-to-end examples exist in /examples/sdk/sessioned_tool_flow for TS, Py, Go and are runnable in CI smoke tests.
Security review completed and session-token telemetry added to audit logs.
